flashcard_questions.q: A coastline where rock layers run parallel to the shore, so waves hit the same rock type.
A coastline where different rock types run at right angles to the shore, so waves erode each type at a different rate.
A wide, curved indentation in the coastline formed by the erosion of softer rock between two areas of harder rock.

flashcard_questions.a: A narrow area of hard rock that sticks out into the sea, formed because it resists erosion more than the surrounding softer rock.
A low remnant of rock left after a stack has been eroded and collapsed.
